newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker but evade New York's drop.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker but evade New York's drop.

text.p: Toronto's stock market ended weaker in moderate dealings on Friday amid profit-taking and double-witching, but managed to avoid Wall Street's steep drop.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slid 29.27 points to 6247.38 while the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 139 points to close at 7195.

"People going into a weekend, whether long or short, want to take profits," said Fred Ketchen, director of trading at ScotiaMcLeod. Canadian markets will be closed on Monday for the Victoria Day holiday.
Trading was moderate at 88.7 million shares worth C$1.36 billion ($993 million).
Ketchen said that double witching, the expiration of options and futures, added to volatility in both markets.

In Toronto, heavyweight golds lost 1.6 percent on weak bullion prices. "We can't get any long-term or consistent news out of the gold sector," Ketchen said. New York's June prices on COMEX closed $3.50 lower at $346.30.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices weakened except for retail and utilities. Gold stocks were the top losers, followed by real estate, banks, media and transportation.
Declining stocks outpaced advances 380 to 328, while 262 issues were flat.
Canada's largest stock market ended the week nearly flat from Monday's opening level of 6239.04 points with today's losses offsetting earlier gains.
Among individual issues, shares in gold prospector Golden Rule Resources Ltd. fell 3.46, or nearly 47 percent, to close at 3.94 on 2.6 million shares.

The company has hired a consultant to review its gold joint venture in Ghana after check assay reports for the Ghana Minerals Commission suggested Golden Rule's assay results for the site were overstated.
Pure Gold Resources Inc. lost 0.09 to close at 0.41 on 7.0 million shares after the release of drill results from a joint venture diamond project in Alberta.
